ccc6Previews.name: Scotland, Wales, NI assumptions
preview: This tab provides a description of the methodologies used to disaggregate UK scenarios for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
Methodology for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland

• Road vehicle traffic (including HGVs) is based on the Department for Transport’s (DfT) National Transport Model (NTM), which produces forecasts by GB country. The NTM model does not include Northern Ireland, so emissions there are scaled based on current vehicle-km use by vehicle type.
• National Travel Survey (NTS) data are no longer collected, but our assumption on UK-average changes in travel behaviour is not expected to have a significant impact on DAs’ emissions pathways.

• Our analysis uses a model of the GB network only. To allocate electricity supply emissions to Scotland and Wales, we sum the existing plant-level capacity and projected retirement dates for each generating technology and apply load factors to these based on changes in GB-wide load factors. For Northern Ireland, we forecast demand due to increased electrification and combine this with the Northern Ireland grid emission intensity from the most recent System Operator Northern Ireland (SONI) report.

ccc6Previews.name: Buildings additional data
preview: Additional data behind the buildings pathways
Explanatory notes for non-residential buildings analysis:

Operating costs included in the data-book are based on changes in fuel costs only and do not include changes in maintenance costs. Both fuel costs and maintenance costs have been included alongside capital costs in estimating abatement costs for heat and energy efficiency measures.
Abatement costs for catering and other non-heat purposes have been estimated based on changes in fuel costs only.
In the Headwinds scenario, there is an additional 9.6 TWh demand for hydrogen in non-residential buildings district heat by 2050, which is costed but omitted in the energy totals.
Abatement for each measure is based on CO2 emissions. Non-CO2 abatement of all measures has been calculated in aggregate and in the data-book is included within the ‘catering and other’ category.
A decarbonisation trajectory has not been developed for the 0.6MtCOe of N2O emissions arising from use of anaesthetics in health care.
